rows.note: Use this formal abstract noun when discussing how pressing a matter is, rather than the everyday adjective 急.

example.english: The urgency of this matter is obvious, so we need to hurry.
example.traditional: 呢件事嘅迫切性好明顯，我哋要快啲處理。
example.jyutping: ni1 gin6 si6 ge3 bik1 cit3 sing3 hou2 ming4 hin2 ngo5 dei6 jiu3 faai3 di1 cyu5 lei5

rows.note: This is the all-purpose everyday choice for hurrying or trying to get something done quickly.

example.english: We need to hurry and finish this homework.
example.traditional: 我哋要趕住做完呢份功課。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 jiu3 gon2 zyu6 zou6 jyun4 ni1 fan6 gung1 fo3

rows.note: Use this specifically when speeding up the rate or progress of an activity or process rather than simply rushing.

example.english: The process is too slow—can you hurry it up a bit?
example.traditional: 個程序行得太慢，可唔可以加快少少？
example.jyutping: go3 cing4 zeoi6 haang4 dak1 taai3 maan6 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 gaa1 faai3 siu2 siu2

rows.note: Use this when urging another person or process to proceed or be completed more quickly.

example.english: You don’t need to hurry me; I’ll finish soon.
example.traditional: 你唔使催我，我就快做完喇。
example.jyutping: nei5 m4 sai2 ceoi1 ngo5 ngo5 zau6 faai3 zou6 jyun4 laa3

rows.traditional: 逼到 A 亂晒陣腳
rows.jyutping: bik1 dou3 A lyun6 saai3 zan6 gok3
rows.note: Use this when pressure drives someone into confused, disorganized, or rash action.

example.english: The tight deadline made me hurry and panic, so I even made mistakes in the document.
example.traditional: 時間太趕，逼到我亂晒陣腳，連份文件都寫錯咗。
example.jyutping: si4 gaan3 taai3 gon2 bik1 dou3 ngo5 lyun6 saai3 zan6 gok3 lin4 fan6 man4 gin6 dou1 se2 co3 zo2
